sentences.text: Revenue rose from $26.6 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F10], a 6.2% CAGR [F157].
The path is a step change rather than steady compounding: revenue peaked at $61.3 billion in FY2023 [F8], then fell 15.6% in FY2024 [D367] and 11.7% in FY2025 [D412].
Operating margin rose from 9.7% in FY2016 [F22] to 21.2% in FY2023 [F29], well above the 12.1% window median [D1335].
The largest inflection was FY2021, when revenue grew 23.9% [D231] and operating margin rose 6.1pp [D243], which the filing attributes to higher shipment volumes and price realization [P43].
Production and Precision Agriculture, 38.9% of FY2025 revenue [D867], contributed -7.0pp to the revenue change [D869], a bigger drag than Construction & Forestry's -3.0pp [D891].
The filing attributes the segment's fall to a 30% drop in U.S. and Canada volumes, partly offset by growth in Brazil [P10][D869].
Small Agriculture & Turf declined 7.0% in FY2025 [D906], with U.S. and Canada volumes down 17% [P9].
Operating expenses fell 7.3% [D425] against an 11.7% revenue decline [D412], a 4.4pp gap [D431], so cost cuts did not offset lower volume.
Diluted EPS fell 27.8% [D415], less than the 29.2% fall in net income [D413], as the diluted share count shrank 1.9% [D427].
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median [D1335] but 3.7pp lower year on year [D378].
SG&A accounts for 1.9pp [D391] and R&D for 0.9pp [D390] of that fall, with other lines adding 0.9pp [D392].
Material costs fell, but manufacturing overhead rose on lower volumes and production inefficiencies [P16][D378].
In FY2021 margin rose 6.1pp [D243], with SG&A adding 2.1pp [D256], R&D 1.0pp [D255] and other lines 3.0pp [D257].
R&D was 5.1% of FY2025 revenue [D393], above the 4.5% window median [D1344] and at the 100th percentile of industrials peers [D1355].
Free cash flow of $6.1 billion [F100] was 1.21x net income [D402], against a 0.91x window median [D1347].
Operating cash flow of $7.5 billion [F80] reflected net income adjusted for non-cash items and lower receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Capex was 3.0% of FY2025 revenue [D397] and 0.61x depreciation [D403], below FY2024's 0.77x [D358].
Conversion was weakest in FY2022 at 0.66x [D266], when the filing cites higher receivables, inventory build and a voluntary OPEB contribution [P27].
Net debt narrowed to $5.5 billion in FY2025 [D407], or 12.1% of revenue [D408], from $10.5 billion in FY2023 [D317].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of industrials peers on net cash to revenue [D1357], against a peer median of -38.8% [D1358].
Buybacks plus dividends were $2.9 billion in FY2025 [D409], 46.9% of free cash flow [D410], down from 121.9% in FY2023 [D320].
Diluted shares fell 1.9% in FY2025 [D427], but return on average equity of 20.6% [D411] ranks at the 17th percentile of six peers, against a 28.3% median [D1361][D1362].
Revenue has fallen for two straight years, the highest-severity flag in the pack [R1][F9][F10].
The FY2024 filing ties lower shipments to rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates [P17][D367].
The FY2025 filing says the allowance grew on higher expected losses in agriculture and turf accounts [P4], with the provision still $296.0 million [X171] against $310.0 million in FY2024 [X170].
Production and Precision Agriculture is 38.9% of revenue [D867] and fell 17.0% in FY2025 [D868], a concentration risk [R3].
In the FY2026 10-K, a recovery above Production and Precision Agriculture's FY2025 revenue of $17.8 billion [S213] would reverse the decline, while a fall below it would confirm the trend.
Management forecasts lower equipment operating cash flow in 2026 [P6]; an FY2026 figure below FY2025's $7.5 billion [F80] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm that forecast.
A provision above FY2024's $310.0 million [X170] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm rising credit pressure, while a fall below FY2025's $296.0 million [X171] would support recovery.
